messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty: HIGH — GPU memory pressure in pool infer-west-2a. 85%+ util sustained for 7m, 3 CUDA OOMs in last 2m. Ticket PD#12345. Links: https://pagerduty.example/PD12345

alice (oncall): acked. I'm jumping in — checking node health and recent allocations.

bob (infra): seeing repeated `CUDARuntimeError: out of memory` from containers on node gw-infer-12. KV cache size spiked.

carol (sre): local metrics: `gpu_mem_used/gpu_mem_total` shows 0.88, and GPU reclaim isn't keeping up. Few long-running rerank jobs saw token spikes.

alice (oncall): provisional impact: ~14 requests failing with 500s in the last 5m, some latency spikes. Notified support.

dave (support): I'm pinging the two customers with high qps that hit the failures. Will update if they report outages.

alice (oncall): mitigation plan: 1) enable auto-evac on pool to move lower-priority jobs 2) scale burst pool by +2 g4dn 3) force fallback to smaller model variant for traffic route `prod-infer`

bob (infra): running drain on gw-infer-12 now:```bash
kubectl cordon node/gw-infer-12
kubectl drain node/gw-infer-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```

ops-bot: Node gw-infer-12 cordoned, 7 pods evicted.

carol (sre): kicking the evict + restart of inference service on that host. Also reducing KV cache target to 64MB for that pool:```yaml
pool: infer-west-2a
kv_cache_target: 64MB
```

alice (oncall): switching route `prod-infer` to model `rwd-medium-v1-quant` as a temporary fallback to reduce memory per-request.```http
POST /route/update
{ "route": "prod-infer", "model": "rwd-medium-v1-quant", "weight": 100 }
```

bob (infra): launched 2 extra nodes (gw-infer-20, gw-infer-21) in warm pool. Autoscaler triggered an extra allocation, ETA ~90s.

carol (sre): monitoring: OOMs dropped to 0 after evict, memory util fell to ~65% on remaining nodes. Latency normalizing.

alice (oncall): good. Support, any customer alerts yet?

dave (support): Customer A reported errors but back to normal after ~2m. They're on the smaller fallback now. Customer B saw degraded latency, no error pages. Logged incident emails.

alice (oncall): PD#12345 acknowledged and being tracked. We'll keep fallback active for 20m then attempt gradual rollback. Adding note to runbook: https://docs.redwood/ops/runbooks/gpu-oom

ops-bot: PD#12345 status -> acknowledged by alice (oncall). Escalation timer paused.

bob (infra): follow-up action items: - Investigate KV cache growth root cause (possibly prefetch storm) - Add more aggressive KV eviction threshold to pool - Add rate limiters to rerank jobs by token length

carol (sre): creating a postmortem stub: "infer-west-2a memory pressure — prefetch/kvcache spike caused OOMs; mitigated via node drain, fallback, and scale-up." I'll flesh with metrics and timelines.

alice (oncall): handing off to bob for deep-dive. If anything regresses, re-open PD. For now I'll un-ack if noise returns. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

bob (infra): taking handoff — will follow up with logs and a candidate patch to cap prefetch.

incident-bot: PD#12345 updated: status -> monitoring.

alice (oncall): closing active coordination in this thread. Final: impacted ~2 customers briefly, no broader outage. Root cause investigation assigned to bob.

carol (sre): adding timeline notes: root alert 1799998888, mitigation started +2m, node drained +4m, scale-up +6m, memory stable +8m.

ops-bot: Incident summary posted to #incidents-kanban card ID INC-9876.

alice (oncall): thumbs: :white_check_mark: — marking as resolved in channel, leaving followups in the postmortem.
